source.title: Analytic Study of Families of Spurious Minima in Two-Layer ReLU Neural Networks

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no garbling or cutoff affecting the reported findings is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analytically studies spurious minima and their Hessians in a finite two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem, bearing on V2's question about spurious minima, but does not test gradient-descent convergence rates or the width comparison in V2.
record.gate_note: Reports analytically derived families of global and spurious minima and gives empirical examples obtained by SGD. It does not report how often gradient descent ends in spurious minima as teacher and student grow together, or compare student widths one or two neurons above teacher width. Results cited from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own SGD runs reach spurious minima in a realizable two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem. These examples bear on V2's optimizer-failure component, but do not test failure frequencies as width grows or the benefit of one or two extra neurons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: symmetry-based analysis characterizes spurious-minimum families and shows that their Hessian spectra agree with global-minimum spectra to O(d−1/2). Preliminary experiments suggest that increasing student width at fixed input dimension turns spurious minima into saddles; a thorough study is deferred.
record.recipe_differences: Population squared-loss teacher-student setting with Gaussian inputs and analytic characterization of minima; empirical examples use SGD. It is not the CIFAR classification recipe or the teacher-student width sweep in V2.
record.method_sensitivity: The analytically described critical-point families depend on dimension and symmetry type. The authors state that increasing the number of student neurons while fixing input dimension can turn spurious minima into saddles, based on preliminary experiments without a quantified sweep in this text.

fits_no_version.finding: Analytically characterized spurious-minimum families have losses that either decay as Θ(1/d) or approach 1/2 − 1/π.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Realizable finite two-layer ReLU population-loss landscapes contain distinct families of positive-loss local minima.

fits_no_version.finding: Spurious minima adapt their symmetry to modified target networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spurious minima can inherit subgroups of the target network's symmetry.

fits_no_version.finding: Preliminary experiments indicate that increasing student width at fixed input dimension turns families of spurious minima into saddles; no widths or optimizer-failure rates are supplied.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing student width can destabilize existing spurious-minimum families.

fits_no_version.finding: Global and spurious minima have Hessian spectra agreeing to O(d−1/2), and a critical-point family changes stability near fractional dimension 5.71.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local Hessian spectra can fail to distinguish global from spurious minima, while dimension changes critical-point stability.

record.problems: The SGD examples are limited to k = d = 10 and are illustrative; the text does not report seeds, success frequency, or a width sweep. The claimed over-parameterized annihilation of spurious minima is described as preliminary, with experiments and rigorous study deferred. The main analytic results concern expected squared loss on Gaussian inputs, not benchmark classification error.
record.rows_left_out: None. The paper's theorem also gives the global minimum in case 1a with loss 0, but it is not a spurious-minimum result bearing on V2. Hessian eigenvalue tables and discussion do not measure the gradient-descent width-frequency claim in V2.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and size or training-duration comparisons.

Failure frequencies under standard initialization; increasing teacher and student widths together; and whether one or two extra student neurons sharply reduce optimizer failures. Selected SGD examples establish occurrence, without estimating prevalence.
Depth-related training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, deep tanh initialization, or Fixup.
Initialization effects on training speed, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth. The qualitative Xavier-initialization observation concerns which minima are selected.
Learning-rate thresholds, transient loss growth, recovery, divergence, and curvature during training.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V2. The analytic landscape results and preliminary saddle-conversion observation do not establish V2's quantitative optimizer-frequency or one-or-two-extra-neuron claims. The supplied theorem formulas contain substantial extraction corruption despite the record's file-quality assessment.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, convolutional networks, SGD/Adam training from random initialization, and effects of model size or training duration.

The paper establishes families of spurious minima analytically and provides examples, but does not measure gradient descent's frequency of ending in spurious minima across growing teacher/student widths or test students with one or two extra neurons.
Plain versus residual networks, depth, shortcuts, normalization, and training error.
Initialization comparisons, signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability, loss dynamics, and curvature during training.
Batch-normalization comparisons and training speed or learning-rate tolerance.
